item.title: Why 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw was fined $12,537 after San Francisco was upset by Falcons
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Why 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw was fined $12,537 after San Francisco was upset by Falcons appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL has fined San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw $12,537 over an incident involving Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London in their Week 7 29-20 loss , NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday. The league penalized the 29-year-old for unnecessary roughness after an attempted forced fumble resulted in a punch to London’s helmet. Greenlaw attempted to knock the football loose as London advanced with a reception from quarterback Michael Penix in the red zone. However, London ducked while securing possession, causing Greenlaw’s punch to connect with his helmet rather than the ball. Although officials did not throw a flag during the play, the league reviewed the incident and subsequently issued its financial penalty. London left the game to undergo a concussion evaluation following the contact but was eventually cleared to return. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This marks Greenlaw’s second fine of the 2026 season. Earlier in the season, he was fined $11,941 after exchanging taunts with the Denver Broncos’ sideline and head coach Sean Payton, who had been his former coach before the Broncos released him. Greenlaw has also faced additional disciplinary action this year. He received a one-game suspension following a sideline confrontation with Seattle Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV during Week 5. Greenlaw headbutted Jones, who was not wearing a helmet at the time. Although he appealed the punishment, the NFL upheld its decision, forcing him to miss the team’s Week 6 meeting with the Washington Commanders. Greenlaw’s disciplinary history also includes previous suspensions. He missed time after a helmet-to-helmet hit on Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert and received another one-game suspension in 2025 following a confrontation with referee Brad Allen, whom he reportedly verbally threatened after a loss. Meanwhile, Greenlaw was not the only San Francisco player penalized for his actions against the Falcons. Second-year running back Jordan James received a $6,194 fine for unnecessary roughness involving the use of his helmet. The 49ers now have their bye week before returning to action against the Las Vegas Raiders on November 8 at Levi’s Stadium. item.title: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics: How To Watch And Who To Watch
item.description: A torchbearer carries the Youth Olympic Flame during the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games at the Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio on October 31, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Africa has opened its first ever Olympic Games as Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye declared the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games open on Saturday night at the 55,000-capacity Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio, with IOC President Kirsty Coventry in attendance. More than 1,000 performers took part in the opening ceremony, which included the presence of two Senegalese teenagers, fencer Abdourahmane Marième Sy and judoka Aïcha Diop, to light the cauldron with the Olympic flame as it concluded its journey on African soil for the first time. The Games were first awarded for 2022 and pushed back four years by the pandemic, with dates being further pushed back due to delays in preparations. Having opened on October 31st, they now run until November 13. Here is what is on, when to watch it from the US, who to follow and what it all costs. Dakar 2026 at a glance Around 2,655 athletes aged 14 to 17 are competing, representing 204 national teams. There are 153 medal events across 25 sports, plus 10 “engagement” sports where young people can try disciplines without medals on the line. Dakar is the first Youth Olympics with full gender parity, with 1,350 quota places each for boys and girls, and it is also the first Youth Games to include a Refugee Olympic Team, with six athletes competing in athletics, judo and taekwondo. Competition is split across three hubs. Dakar hosts athletics, swimming, futsal and the urban sports, Diamniadio, a new city about 20 miles from the capital, has the main stadium and the athletes’ village, while the beach resort of Saly, on Senegal’s Petite Côte, hosts beach sports, rowing and triathlon. Two sports are making their Youth Olympic debut. Baseball5, a five-a-side street version of baseball that needs no bats or gloves, opened competition on October 30th, a day before the opening ceremony. Wushu taolu, a Chinese martial art judged on routines, is also making its debut. Street skateboarding, break dancing, beach wrestling and coastal rowing sprints round out a programme built with a younger audience in mind in terms of both participation and viewing. Ayo, the mascot of Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. AFP via Getty Images How to watch the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games US viewers have two routes, and one of them is free for users. NBC Olympics holds the US rights, and Peacock is streaming selected sessions live. Peacock’s listings for the first week include boys’ and girls’ rugby sevens from November 1st to 3rd. They also include the beach volleyball gold medal matches at 8:55 a.m. ET and the men’s street skateboarding final at 11 a.m. ET, both on Wednesday, November 4th. item.title: “What A Loser” – Serena Williams’ Coach Reacts After Journalist Debunks Vivek Ramaswamy’s ‘Nationally Ranked’ Tennis Claim
item.description: Rennae Stubbs (left) and Serena Williams (right) © Instagram/@rennaestubbs Serena Williams’ coach Rennae Stubbs reacted after a journalist called out Vivek Ramaswamy’s claim of being a nationally ranked junior tennis player. The claim that Ramaswamy was a nationally ranked junior tennis player appeared in several campaign profiles and online biographies, including Wikipedia, and became part of his public image during his political campaigns, especially during his run for Ohio governor. However, journalist Pablo Torre challenged Ramaswamy’s claim on his podcast, saying the USTA (United States Tennis Association) had no record of him being nationally ranked as a junior player. Instead, the USTA listed him at No. 48 in the boys’ under-16 Midwest regional rankings in its 2002 yearbook. “We can bring in some reporting trying to fact-check this,” Torre said. “The US Tennis Association has no records of him being a nationally ranked junior tennis player, period. And when I reached out to the USA myself, they sent me every one of their yearbooks from the 1990s and the 2000s. And it is very clear based on these records, which they double checked for PTFO, that Ramaswamy was never noted to be nationally ranked. But his name does appear once not nationally but regionally in the 2002 yearbook when he finished according to the reporting now in front of you DJ and he finished uh number 48 in the boys 16 and under division of the Midwest section of the USA. Number 48 out of 50.” After Torre uncovered the claims, Serena Williams’ coach reacted, writing: “Also Pablo, the chances of him hitting a 120 mph serve IN THE COURT is zero.” She also referred to Ramaswamy as a loser and added: “Who lies about being ranked in juniors!! What a loser.” Ramaswamy’s campaign has also included a now-deleted video filmed at a batting cage. item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Gabby Williams took over in Game 7 to get the Golden State Valkyries their first-ever WNBA championship and fans were quick to praise her. Gabby Williams has become a WNBA superstar this year. Very few players have ascended as quickly as she has. The Golden State Valkyries acquired her in 2026, and in just her first season, she has become a champion and been named as the Finals MVP. item.title: Kika Nazareth vuelve a lesionarse
item.description: Kika Nazareth vuelve a lesionarse La portuguesa sufre una lesión muscular en el recto anterior de la pierna derecha y estará de baja entre cuatro y cinco semanas Kika Nazareth vuelve a estar en el dique seco. La futbolista portuguesa sufre una l esión miofibrilar del recto anterior de la pierna derecha , según informó el FC Barcelona este domingo. El club estima que estará de baja entre cuatro y cinco semanas . La lesión llega justo cuando la atacante empezaba a recuperar sensaciones después de su anterior problema físico. Ante el HB Køge, Kika participó en la goleada azulgrana por 0-8 , marcó un gol y dio una asistencia en menos de media hora sobre el terreno de juego. Kika Nazareth durante un partido del Barça en el Johan Cruyff. Fuente: 3Cat Se perderá varios partidos La nueva lesión apartará a la centrocampista de varios compromisos importantes del Barça . La portuguesa no estará ante el Badalona Women, Madrid CFF, Deportivo y Athletic Club en Liga F . Tampoco podrá participar en los partidos de Champions League contra el Arsenal y el Servette . Su ausencia supone un nuevo contratiempo para Pere Romeu , que pierde a una jugadora que apenas comenzaba a recuperar continuidad después de una temporada marcada por los problemas físicos. Otro problema en la misma zona El nuevo contratiempo supone la tercera lesión de Kika desde que llegó al club catalán y vuelve a afectar al mismo músculo. En septiembre, la portuguesa ya sufrió una lesión mioaponeurótica del recto anterior de la pierna derecha . Ahora, dos meses después, vuelve a tener afectada esa zona. La atacante reconoció tras el partido ante el HB Køge que estaba feliz por haber regresado a la dinámica del equipo. Por fin he vuelto, tenía muchas ganas. Sin embargo, tendrá que volver a parar durante varias semanas. Romeu recurre a la cantera La baja de la portuguesa se suma a las de Irene Paredes, Vicky López y Laia Aleixandri , que continúan con sus respectivos procesos de recuperación. Ante esta situación, el técnico azulgrana ha tenido que recurrir al filial para completar la convocatoria del derbi contra el Badalona Women . Julia Torres, Noa Jiménez, Rosalía Domínguez y Mayssa Baha son las cuatro jugadoras del Barça Atlètic citadas para el encuentro. Romeu tendrá que gestionar una plantilla cada vez más condicionada por las bajas. - Publicidad -

item.title: 'I was just waiting for that moment': Fakhar Zaman after Pakistan match India's 2002 Lord's record
item.description: Fakhar Zaman had gone through four matches without the kind of performance he wanted. But the Pakistan opener knew that a big innings was around the corner. He just had to wait for the right moment. That moment arrived in the One-Day International tri-series final against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday. Zaman smashed 127 off 99 balls to help Pakistan chase down 326 and win the final by three wickets. Pakistan finished at 331 for seven in 48.3 overs, with nine balls to spare. It was a special victory for the hosts, who also equalled India's famous record for the highest successful chase in an ODI final. Speaking after winning the Player of the Match award, Zaman explained how he dealt with his lack of runs in the previous four matches and why he never changed his approach. 'I was just waiting for that moment' Zaman admitted that he was not at his best at the start of the final. However, he continued to trust his preparation and believed that a big score would come when he found his rhythm. "No, look, I've played enough cricket now to know that when it's my day and the ball starts coming nicely off my bat, I'll score big. So I was just waiting for that moment. I didn't do anything particularly different from the way I had approached the previous four matches. I prepared for this game in exactly the same way. But that's the thing: when you score runs, we start talking about how mentally ready you were, how your fitness was and all of that. I prepared for this match in the same way I had prepared for the other games. Luckily, the runs came today," Zaman said. The left-hander also spoke about his struggles at the beginning of the innings and how important the century was for him. "Look, the way my first four matches had gone, I felt a good performance was due, and I was putting in the effort. But cricket is such a game that sometimes you're in really good touch, but the runs just don't come. Even today, I was struggling a little at the start, but luckily the runs came, and that's a good thing for me. Whenever there is a final, I seem to score runs," he said. Pakistan were in trouble early in the chase after Dilshan Madushanka dismissed Babar Azam for a five-ball duck. The Sri Lankan pacer also picked up another wicket in the powerplay. Zaman then joined Saad Baig, and the two rebuilt the innings with a 149-run partnership. Baig scored 74 off 75 balls, registering his maiden ODI half-century. Zaman said his young teammate's approach allowed him to take his time at the other end. "I've played domestic cricket with him as well, and he's a very talented player. item.title: Alex Marquez skips controversial Qatar GP to undergo surgery
item.description: Motorsport photo Alex Marquez has confirmed that he will miss next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix in favour of surgery. The possibility was revealed by Motorsport.com yesterday . Marquez then announced it was a certainty in the press conference following his third place in today's Malaysian Grand Prix. The operation, which will take place in Madrid on Monday, is to deal with the ongoing consequences of Marquez's massive crash in the Catalan Grand Prix in May. Read Also: How Alex Marquez experienced his brutal crash in Catalan GP The younger Marquez is hopeful of a return to action for the Portuguese Grand Prix at Portimao in three weeks. "From the moment that I came back after the Catalonia accident, I suffered a lot with my right shoulder," said the Gresini Ducati rider. "And yeah, I decided to take surgery in Madrid tomorrow. "I will try to come back in Portimao. Speaking with the doctors a little bit, that's possible. "I need to take out the plate from the collarbone, but the main problem I have now is the inflammation. So, it's like two surgeries in one. "The main thing will be trying to extract all the inflammation, all the liquid that I have on the right shoulder. Because now, you know, I can't do any work at home. I don't have muscle, I don't have nothing. "So, as I said, [I will] step back, take time to rest a little bit, and try to make, in a proper way, the final two races of the season." Alex Marquez after the race at Sepang Alex Marquez after the race at Sepang Cynics may suggest that the reluctance of riders to race in Qatar makes the timing of the surgery particularly convenient. But Marquez says that Qatar being the third race in a triple-header is a major factor. "I was suffering a lot with these back-to-back races. So for me, it's impossible to do three in a row. So, I decided to step back a little bit. "I was racing with painkillers and all that, but you know, already now, even that was not enough. So, it's time to do that surgery and try to come back stronger in Portimao and Valencia." item.title: Pokemon celebration: Blair Tickner celebrates uniquely after dismissing Naman Dhir in 5th T20I at Hamilton
item.description: Pokemon celebration: Blair Tickner celebrates uniquely after dismissing Naman Dhir in 5th T20I at Hamilton originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: New Zealand pacer Blair Tickner pulled out a Pokemon card to celebrate dismissing Naman Dhir in Hamilton. The card carried a fire energy icon. Tickner finished with 2/38 as India posted 191/8 in their twenty overs. WATCH: Blair Tickner’s bizarre Pokémon celebration after removing Naman Dhir in 5th T20I Blair Tickner found a very different way to celebrate the dismissal of Naman Dhir in the fifth T20I by producing a Pokemon card from his pocket. Once the usual huddle had broken up, Tickner reached into his pocket and took out an official Pokemon trading card with a red fire energy symbol on it. He held it up proudly towards the broadcast cameras, and as a final touch he planted a kiss on the card before putting it away again. The wicket itself mattered a great deal, because Dhir had been batting well and looked set to push India past 200 on his own until Tickner removed him for 33 off 23 balls. Dhir had survived a few moments of good fortune before this ball, but his luck ran out in the 19th over. Tickner sent down a knuckle ball outside off stump, and Dhir tried to hit it out of Hamilton, only to get a top edge that went high into the air. Michael Bracewell was stationed at extra cover, and he back-pedalled, dived and held on to a superb catch. By the time the innings was finished, India had posted 191/8 in 20 overs, with half-centuries from Ishan Kishan and quick runs from Shreyas Iyer. Even so, it was the card, and not the total, that had most people talking on social media. Energy cards are the fuel of that game, because a player has to attach them to a Pokemon in order to use its attacks. item.title: Arsenal 20yo suffers ankle injury after returning from ACL lay-off
item.description: Arsenal 20yo suffers ankle injury after returning from ACL lay-off Katie Reid has suffered another setback in her return to action, with Arsenal now facing a longer wait before the defender will be available. Photo by Harry Murphy/Getty Images Katie Reid is facing another spell on the sidelines after picking up an ankle injury just as she had returned to training with Arsenal following her ACL injury. Renée Slegers has confirmed the defender is not expected back before Christmas, putting the brakes on a comeback which had reached the point where Reid was finally training with the rest of the squad again. Speaking at her pre- Aston Villa press conference, Slegers said : “Katie Reid, she was back training with the team, she got an ankle injury, which sets her back, which is unfortunate, so we don’t expect her to be back before Christmas.” She added: “That’s unfortunate for her and that’s a setback. Otherwise, the rest is the same as last night.” There was better news elsewhere. Kim Little returned to action in the Champions League , while Frida Maanum could also be close to making her comeback. Photo by Sarah Ray-Gain/Getty Images “Kim was back last night, which was great to get her back onto the pitch,” Slegers said. “There might be a chance Frida Maanum makes it for the game as well. Daphne van Domselaar is getting closer and closer. Maybe a game too early.” Chloe Kelly remains unavailable, with Arsenal continuing to assess her after a specialist appointment for the hamstring problem that has plagued her since the end of September. Slegers was unable to give a firm timescale there either. Photo by Sarah Ray-Gain/Getty Images “It’s hard to set a clear timeline,” she said. “It’s still day-by-day, seeing how the symptoms are, what we can and can’t do, had a specialist appointment a couple of days ago. “Let’s see where we go from here, but she’s not available for the weekend.” For Reid, though, the latest setback is particularly difficult given that she had already worked her way back to first team training after a year out. photo via Arsenal.com

item.title: ‘I Was Done After Last Year’ — Charles Barkley Reveals How Ernie Johnson Talked Him Into Returning to ‘Inside the NBA’ on ESPN for 1 Final Season
item.description: Charles Barkley opens up about Ernie Johnson’s role in keeping him on Inside the NBA and what Johnson’s retirement means for the show. Charles Barkley had already made up his mind about leaving “Inside the NBA” when its run on TNT came to an end. He wasn’t particularly interested in starting over with another network. But a conversation with longtime co-host Ernie Johnson changed his plans. With Johnson now preparing to leave the show himself, the Hall of Famer’s decision to return has taken on new significance. Charles Barkley Says Ernie Johnson Persuaded Him to Stay on “Inside the NBA” During an Oct. 1 appearance on “In the Trenches with Damien Woody,” the 1993 NBA MVP explained why he was ready to walk away after TNT lost its NBA broadcasting rights. “I was done after last year, and I think Ernie was done. We lost a package to NBC,” Barkley recalled. “And we both met with NBC, and I met with Amazon. I’m like, ‘You know what? I’m good. I’m 63 years old. I’m good.’” The NBA’s new 11-year, $76 billion media agreement with Disney, NBC and Amazon ended TNT’s long-running NBA coverage. “Inside the NBA” subsequently moved to ESPN and ABC under a licensing arrangement, with TNT Sports continuing to produce the show from Atlanta. Johnson called after learning that ESPN wanted to carry the program. The conversation soon turned to the show’s production staff. “And then I get a call from Ernie telling us that ESPN wants to buy the show, and I said, ‘What do you think?’” Barkley said. “He said, ‘Well, we talking a couple hundred people get to keep their jobs.’” The prospect of keeping those employees working convinced Sir Charles to reconsider, although he made it clear that he didn’t want to spend the rest of his life on television. “I would consider that if everybody’s going to keep their job. But Ernie, I don’t want to drop dead on TV. I want to drop dead on the 13th fairway,” he joked. The 11-time All-Star had already indicated that his return wouldn’t be indefinite. During a September appearance on “The Bill Simmons Podcast,” he described himself and Johnson as a package deal and said the 2026-27 season would be his last unless Johnson changed his mind. On October 28, Johnson announced that he would step away from “Inside the NBA” after 37 seasons as host. He emphasized that the decision was his own and that he felt it was time to leave the program. His announcement did not mean he was retiring from television altogether. item.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to extend MotoGP lead
item.description: Marc Marquez won the first of his seven MotoGP titles in 2013 [Getty Images] Reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix to take a 44-point lead over title rival Jorge Martin, who missed the race with injury. It was Marquez's first win in Malaysia since 2018, while his brother Alex finished third behind Pedro Acosta. Marquez, who has won the MotoGP championship seven times, moved up to 399 points after winning by over four seconds. The Spaniard will seal the title with two rounds remaining if he is able to extend his lead to 74 points at the Qatar Grand Prix next week. "We did a perfect race, so I'm super, super happy," said Marquez. "But my mentality still cannot change. I have to keep focus, keep pushing. There are not many races to go, but there are many moments left. So, we must be super confident." The Marquez brothers scrapped for the lead early in the race before the eventual winner pulled ahead, leaving Alex to tussle for the remaining podium places with Acosta. Marquez's compatriot Martin, who won the championship in 2024, tried to ride in the morning practice session but had to withdraw as he struggled with the fractured wrist suffered during a crash at last week's Australian Grand Prix.
